stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In the 1990s, field linguists began recording the last fluent speakers of a small language spoken in the Andean highlands. As they transcribed hours of conversation, the researchers noticed one grammatical feature that set the language apart from its neighbors______ a set of verb endings that marked whether the speaker had personally witnessed the event being described.
explanation: The words before the blank form a complete sentence that points forward to "one grammatical feature" without naming it. The words after the blank are a noun phrase that names that feature. A colon is the right mark to join a complete sentence to a phrase that explains or specifies it.

B.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon needs a complete sentence on both sides, but "a set of verb endings..." has no main verb. It is only a noun phrase.

C.why: Adding "it was" turns the second part into a complete sentence, so a bare comma now joins two complete sentences. That is a comma splice.

D.why: A period makes "A set of verb endings that marked..." its own sentence, but it has no main verb, so it is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: For decades, the kelp forests off central California shrank as purple sea urchins multiplied and grazed the seaweed down to bare rock. When marine biologists compared stretches of coastline where the forests had rebounded with stretches where they had not, they identified the factor most responsible for the recovery______ the return of sea otters, predators that eat large numbers of urchins each day.
explanation: The words before the blank are a complete sentence that promises to name "the factor most responsible." What follows the blank, "the return of sea otters...," is a noun phrase that names that factor. A colon introduces exactly this kind of explanation.

A.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon must join two complete sentences, and "the return of sea otters..." is only a noun phrase with no main verb.

B.why: "It was the return of sea otters..." is a complete sentence, so joining it to the first sentence with only a comma creates a comma splice.

D.why: A period leaves "The return of sea otters, predators that eat..." standing alone. It has no main verb, so it is a sentence fragment.

The observations revealed something far more surprising______ a thin ring of icy debris circling Quaoar at a distance where, according to existing models, such material should have clumped together into a moon.
explanation: "The observations revealed something far more surprising" is a complete sentence that sets up an unnamed "something." The noun phrase after the blank names it. A colon correctly joins a complete sentence to the phrase that specifies it.

A.why: Adding "it was" creates a second complete sentence, and a bare comma cannot join two complete sentences. This is a comma splice.

C.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon needs a complete sentence after it, but "a thin ring of icy debris circling Quaoar..." is a noun phrase with no main verb.

D.why: A period turns "A thin ring of icy debris..." into a separate sentence, but it has no main verb. It is a fragment.

explanation: The words before the blank form a complete sentence that points to "one detail" without naming it. The noun phrase after the blank names that detail. A colon correctly joins a complete sentence to the phrase that explains it.

B.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon must be followed by a complete sentence, but "rows of tiny pores called stomata..." has no main verb. The verb "allowed" belongs to the "whose" clause.

C.why: Adding "they were" creates a second complete sentence. Joining two complete sentences with only a comma is a comma splice.

D.why: A period makes "Rows of tiny pores called stomata..." its own sentence, but it has no main verb, so it is a fragment.
